original_source: William Lilly Christian Astrology first edition 1647 Wellcome b30338724
source_limits: Multiple competing methods count legal wives or informal concubines, with many post-hoc escape branches, all historical only.

groups.group: Printed CXXXII heading, watery/fruitful marriage indicators and barren contrast

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXXXII Of the number of Wives
clauses.historical_only_meaning: A separate numbered chapter begins lower original PDF624, after marriage ease and timing chapter.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: all Significators of Marriage be in watry Signes
clauses.historical_only_meaning: Lilly starts from all indicators occupying watery signs rather than merely one watery placement.
The author treats watery signs as traditionally fruitful, not evidence of reproductive physiology.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: for the most part note many Wives
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The text alleges a plural wife count from this condition, without real marital registers.
The author explicitly permits an indefinite multiple outcome instead of a specified number.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: contrary if posited in Virgo Leo Gemini
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The source names Virgo, Leo and Gemini as barren contrast to watery signs for the wife-count method.

groups.group: Moon and Venus, Moon seventh, Saturn/Sun exception and Lilly's personal concubine anecdotes

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon and Venus give most evident testimony
clauses.historical_only_meaning: Lilly explicitly prioritizes Moon/Venus in men’s wife-count method over other marriage factors.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon in seventh in what Signe soever
clauses.historical_only_meaning: A lunar seventh-house placement is asserted to predict multiple partners independent of Moon's zodiac sign.
The author alleges plural wife count from Moon-seventh placement, unsupported by marriage data.
An unusually severe Saturn contact is expressly an exception to the Moon-seventh multiple-wives case.
A severe solar affliction is an alternative exception alongside Saturn, not always both.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: I never knew Native failed plurality of She-friends
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The author claims no remembered failures in women-friend count without enumerated cases or controls.
The self-report admits nonmarital concubines as outcome when not two legal wives; this changes the target.
Lilly expressly admits the Moon-seventh rule did not consistently predict two legal spouses.
A fortified Moon is a further modifier used to rescue the plural legal-wife count.
The source alleges more than one legal wife under the strengthened-Moon version, not verified.

groups.group: Moon conjunct exactly one planet; partile/platick distinction and spouse survivorship

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon conjoyned to one Planet onely
clauses.historical_only_meaning: Moon conjoined to exactly one planetary companion is the precondition of the one-wife branch.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: whether by platick or partill aspect
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The author allows both wider-orb and exact conjunction/aspect categories, without explicit numeric orb sizes.
A sole spouse is the asserted outcome, conflicting with flexible Moon-seventh multiple claims in some charts.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon more strong then that Planet
clauses.historical_only_meaning: Relative lunar strength versus aspecting companion is used for a separate mortality prediction.
The source claims husband lives longer if Moon is stronger, not independent survival evidence.
Reverse planetary-strength ranking forms the opposite death-order source case.
The source claims husband dies first in reverse condition, unsupported by observed couple follow-ups.

groups.group: Moon without bodily conjunction: qualifying direction, applying and partile count, fertile sign multiplier

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon bodily joyned to no Planet
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The author introduces a different counting method only if Moon has no bodily conjunction.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: how many Planets ... aspect her partilly
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The number of qualifying partile aspecting planets is proposed to equal spouse count.
Direct planetary motion is a condition on counted planets.
Combustion of candidate planet excludes it from this branch.
Candidates in the traditional fall dignity are excluded.
Detriment is another source-defined dignity exclusion.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon apply to them not they unto her
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The direction of application matters, an explicit negative for reverse application.
The author excludes Sun from the counted planets in this method, not globally.
The original proposes doubling eligible spouse counts when qualifying aspect planets occupy fruitful signs.

groups.group: Ptolemy's one-form versus bicorporeal rule attributed by Lilly

clauses.historical_only_meaning: Lilly explicitly attributes the next method to Ptolemy; the original Ptolemy source has not yet been cross-verified.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon in a Signe of one forme
clauses.historical_only_meaning: A sign classified as one-form is a precondition for the alleged sole-wife Ptolemaic rule.
The one-form rule additionally requires Moon applying to exactly one planet.
Lilly's Ptolemy-attributed method predicts one wife from that combination, without empirical cases.
A dual-bodied zodiac sign is proposed as an alternative Ptolemaic condition.
The bicorporeal case further requires lunar application to multiple planets.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: many Wives or Marriage oftener then once
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The author permits either simultaneous/number or repeated legal marriage as a flexible outcome.

groups.group: Alternative Midheaven-to-Venus arc planet count when earlier source cases absent

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: If no such thing appeare as formerly mentioned
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The Midheaven-Venus method is a fallback after other methods yield no usable configuration.
The method counts a candidate planet only when direct in motion.
Qualifying planets must also avoid combustion in the ordinary form.
Sun beams are also named as disqualifying proximity.
The original location constraint counts planets lying in a specified Midheaven-to-Venus arc.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: making progresse from mid-heaven towards ascendant
clauses.historical_only_meaning: Counting direction from MC towards Ascendant is explicit and cannot be reversed arbitrarily.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: so many Wives shall Native have
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The author proposes one wife per qualifying planetary count, not an independently verified result.

groups.group: Retrograde or combust planets count after dignity and reception rescue

clauses.historical_only_meaning: The source admits retrograde planets as an exception to the ordinary direct-only fallback rule.
Combust candidates are similarly allowed under additional historic dignity criteria.
A candidate in its own domicile can be restored to eligibility despite retrograde or combust state.
Exaltation is the corresponding alternative essential dignity for exception.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: or mutual Reception of such dignities
clauses.historical_only_meaning: Mutual reception of domicile/exaltation can also restore candidate eligibility.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: account those Planets in number for Wives
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The rule explicitly reintroduces previously excluded candidates into the spouse-number count.

groups.group: Lord seventh partile aspects fallback with retrograde/combust candidates

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: When these rules hold not or use cannot be made
clauses.historical_only_meaning: A further fallback method is provided when earlier count schemes cannot be applied.
The object to receive candidate aspects is the ruler of the seventh house.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: behold Lord seventh with partill aspect
clauses.historical_only_meaning: Exactness of candidate planetary aspects is required, not any broad conjunction.
Retrograde condition does not disqualify planets in this fallback method.
Combustion also does not disqualify candidate planets under this particular fallback.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: from thence collect number of Wives
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The author proposes count by all these eligible aspects rather than Moon sign placement.

groups.group: Lilly's self-described best-tested Moon-sign method, applying vs separating and dignities fallback

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: best approved rule I have hitherto found by experience
clauses.historical_only_meaning: Lilly describes preferred personal experience without audited successes, denominators or negative cases.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: how many Planets there are in Signe Moon is in
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The preferred source counts other planets physically in the Moon's same zodiac sign.
Lunar application to companions is required for the preferred first variant.
Already separating contacts are explicitly excluded from this variant.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: so many Wives Native may expect
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The author maps same-sign applying candidates directly to alleged wife count.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if no such bodily presence be
clauses.historical_only_meaning: A secondary branch applies when Moon has no qualifying bodily contact in her sign.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Planets having dignities in Signe she is in
clauses.historical_only_meaning: Alternative candidates must hold essential dignity in Moon's sign.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: doe behold her with partill aspect
clauses.historical_only_meaning: Those dignity-qualified candidates also must aspect Moon partile, not just occupy a related sign.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: so many Wives may be hoped for
clauses.historical_only_meaning: Lilly concludes the alternative partile/dignity count, without independent outcome verification.

groups.group: Weak signifiers switch wife count target to informal romance; two and three wife conditions

clauses.historical_only_meaning: A weak marriage-significator condition changes what is inferred from the proposed wife-count rules.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: they argue Sweet hearts and Wenches
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The source treats nonlegal relationships as outcome when wife count fails, an explicit target switch.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: may woo for Wives rather then marriage itself
clauses.historical_only_meaning: Attempting to obtain marriage is distinct from actually marrying, another rescue category.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon apply to a Planet in common Signe
clauses.historical_only_meaning: One purported two-wife case requires Moon applying to a planet located in a common sign.
The common-sign source branch asserts exactly two wives, without marriage documents.
The three-wife branch begins with Moon in a fruitful sign.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: apply Planet in fruitful or Bycorporeall Signes
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The Moon must apply to a planet in another fruitful or bicorporeal sign.
The author claims a three-wife total from the lunar/planet sign pair.
A fertile seventh-house sign further strengthens the source's three-wife claim.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord seventh in common or fruitfull Signe
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The seventh ruler must also be in a common/fruitful sign for the stronger version.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: without dispute Native will have three Wives
clauses.historical_only_meaning: Lilly states certainty for the compound three-wife branch despite no independent confirmation.

groups.group: Following CXXXIII spouse origin/quarter navigation only

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXXXIII From whence from what Quarter native shall have Wife
clauses.historical_only_meaning: The next printed numbered chapter begins after divider on original PDF626; subject is spouse birthplace/origin, not wife count.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Significators Marriage in ninth or third houses
clauses.historical_only_meaning: Only the following chapter's opening phrase is preserved for boundary verification.
